dataset_id.description: The ID of the dataset containing this row access policy.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

filter_predicate.description:
A SQL boolean expression that represents the rows defined by this row
access policy, similar to the boolean expression in a WHERE clause of a
SELECT query on a table.
References to other tables, routines, and temporary functions are not
supported.

Examples: region="EU"
date_field = CAST('2019-9-27' as DATE)
nullable_field is not NULL
numeric_field BETWEEN 1.0 AND 5.0
filter_predicate.rationale: A free-form SQL boolean expression defining which rows the policy exposes. Like an embedded policy document, an arbitrary SQL predicate cannot be meaningfully constrained by a generic platform policy, so it is out of scope.

grantees.description:
Input only. The optional list of iam_member users or groups that specifies the initial
members that the row-level access policy should be created with.

grantees types:
- "user:alice@example.com": An email address that represents a specific
Google account.
- "serviceAccount:my-other-app@appspot.gserviceaccount.com": An email
address that represents a service account.
- "group:admins@example.com": An email address that represents a Google
group.
- "domain:example.com":The Google Workspace domain (primary) that
represents all the users of that domain.
- "allAuthenticatedUsers": A special identifier that represents all service
accounts and all users on the internet who have authenticated with a Google
Account. This identifier includes accounts that aren't connected to a
Google Workspace or Cloud Identity domain, such as personal Gmail accounts.
Users who aren't authenticated, such as anonymous visitors, aren't
included.
- "allUsers":A special identifier that represents anyone who is on
the internet, including authenticated and unauthenticated users. Because
BigQuery requires authentication before a user can access the service,
allUsers includes only authenticated users.
grantees.rationale: The list of users/groups granted row-level access. Mis-set to public/wildcard principals (e.g. allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers) it exposes rows broadly; a policy should reject public and wildcard principals while leaving teams free to grant specific users/groups.

policy_id.description:
The ID of the row access policy. The ID must contain only
letters (a-z, A-Z), numbers (0-9), or underscores (_). The maximum
length is 256 characters.
policy_id.rationale: A name/identifier for the row access policy resource. It is just a label and does not control who can see which rows (that is the predicate and grantees), so there is nothing generic to enforce on it.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

table_id.description: The ID of the table containing this row access policy.
